survivors.claim: The last commit in range broke D2's `.claude/worktrees` skip: `walk()` now tests `entry.name === '.claude/worktrees'`, but a directory entry's name never contains a slash, so the branch is dead and every checked-out worktree's tests are counted into the host's number.
survivors.impact: The instrument this spec ships reports a wrong number on any checkout that has worktrees: the ledger row for the main repo reads about eight times the true count, and every future growth-per-spec comparison built on it is noise.
survivors.evidence: D2 quoted: 'a walk that skips .git, node_modules, fixtures, __fixtures__, .claude/worktrees'. Executed repro — fixture with tests/a.test.js (1 case), .claude/worktrees/wt1/tests/b.test.js (2 cases), other/worktrees/tests/d.test.js (1 case): HEAD count-tests.js --json -> {"count":4}; the pre-refactor scanner over the same fixture -> {"count":2}; listTestFiles at HEAD lists .claude/worktrees/wt1/tests/b.test.js. Live: --root <worktree> -> 1021; --root <main repo, five worktrees present> -> 8062. The module's own header (lines 36-38) still says '.claude/worktrees is matched by RELATIVE path' — the comment describes the deleted code. No test pins the worktrees skip, which is why the suite (1050/1050) stayed green.

survivors.claim: The `tests` leg writes {count:0, exit:0} when count-tests.js fails or prints unparseable output, so a broken instrument is recorded as a host with zero tests rather than as an unavailable observation.
survivors.impact: A crashed counter lands on the ledger as a plausible-looking zero instead of a visible gap.
survivors.evidence: Executed: parsing count-tests.js --root /nonexistent --json (child status 2, empty stdout) the way lines 341-344 do yields {"leg":"tests","exit":0,"observed":{"count":0}}.
